description: The line plot illustrates the sparsity ratio of SDPA (Scaled Dot-Product Attention) output across 22 layers of a large language model, comparing three conditions: “before gate” (blue dashed line), “after gate” (orange dotted line), and “after average gate” (green dash-dot line), with their respective average sparsity ratios noted in the legend as 0.003, 0.126, and 0.080. The x-axis, labeled “Layer,” spans from 0 to approximately 22 with linear spacing and tick marks at intervals of 5. The y-axis, labeled “Sparsity Ratio,” ranges from 0.0 to 0.8 with linear scaling and tick marks at 0.2 intervals. The blue dashed line (“before gate”) starts near 0.02 at layer 0 and increases gradually to about 0.38 by layer 22. The orange dotted line (“after gate”) begins near 0.85 at layer 0, drops sharply to around 0.22 by layer 5, fluctuates slightly between 0.2 and 0.3 until layer 15, then rises to approximately 0.4 by layer 22. The green dash-dot line (“after average gate”) starts near 0.8 at layer 0, declines steeply to about 0.18 by layer 5, remains relatively flat near 0.2 until layer 15, then climbs to around 0.38 by layer 22. All three lines show a general trend of decreasing sparsity in early layers followed by a moderate increase in later layers, with the “after gate” condition consistently exhibiting the highest sparsity ratio across most layers.
